solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Old Christian put good money into use after appeal in letter from Athens

indicators.note: putting something into another word means placing it inside that word
after sends the good-and-use section second, behind the appeal and the Greek letter

parts.note: SA is short for sex appeal
tau is a letter of the Greek alphabet
G is the usual abbreviation for good
taken as written; it is split to take the money inside
tin is old slang for money

explanation.surface: An early Christian invests wisely after an appeal in a letter sent from Athens.
explanation.walkthrough: The money goes inside USE, between S and E; 'after' places the good-plus-use section after the appeal-in-letter section.
explanation.definitionFit: The bishop of Hippo was an early Church Father, canonised as a saint, so he is an ancient Christian.

clue.text: Refined aunt reusing set theme songs

indicators.note: something refined has been processed and reworked, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cultured aunt recycles a collection of theme songs.
explanation.definitionFit: A programme's signature tune is the identifying melody that opens it, which is what a theme song is.

clue.text: Girl in Tenerife getting up

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means reading the letters from bottom to top
the answer sits inside the next word of the clue

parts.note: the middle letters of the island's name

explanation.surface: A young woman on holiday in Tenerife is getting out of bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Irene is a female first name, and crosswords often define names by sex alone.

clue.text: Boring book full of wrath finally palls

indicators.note: a thing full of something else holds it inside

parts.note: a tome is a large book

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A dull book full of rage eventually becomes wearisome.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tiresome wears you out with tedium, the same quality as being boring.

clue.text: See 1
Stupid guy ignoring Welsh supporter

indicators.note: ignoring something means leaving it out

parts.note: a wally is British slang for a silly person
W is the abbreviation for Welsh

explanation.surface: A foolish man turns his back on a fan of Welsh rugby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wally' is British slang for a fool; drop its W.
explanation.definitionFit: An ally backs you up, so a supporter is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Old man, upset, angry with a quartet of daughters?

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: four Ds, D being the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: An elderly father is upset and cross about his four daughters.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful counting: four daughters means four Ds.
explanation.definitionFit: Old man is informal for father, and also used for an elderly man; a granddaddy is an old patriarch.

clue.text: Place to rest put in order

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a high-backed wooden bench
second meaning: to sort out or arrange

explanation.surface: Somewhere to rest has been tidied up.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one tidy resting place; the two halves are separate senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: A settle is a wooden seat for resting on, and to settle affairs is to arrange them properly.

clue.text: Possibly licit and ultimately allowable all the same?

indicators.note: possibly suggests one of several arrangements, so the letters may be rearranged
ultimately points to the final letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Is something lawful and finally permitted really just the same thing?
explanation.walkthrough: Licit means lawful, so the surface treats licit and allowable as synonyms, which the question mark mocks.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that are identical are exactly alike, which is what 'all the same' describes.

clue.text: Outrageously starlets demean veteran politician

indicators.note: outrageously means wildly and shockingly, so the letters run riot

explanation.surface: Young actresses shockingly belittle a seasoned politician.
explanation.definitionFit: An elder statesman is a respected senior figure in politics, someone with long experience.

clue.text: One fighting large ape, you say?

indicators.note: you say points to how a word is pronounced rather than spelt

parts.note: the largest ape sounds like an irregular soldier

explanation.surface: Is someone fighting just a big ape?
explanation.definitionFit: A guerrilla is an irregular soldier waging small-scale war, so one who fights.

clue.text: Material originally selected that will engross elegant dowager

indicators.note: originally means at the start, so the opening letters of the words that follow are chosen

parts.note: the initial letters of these five words

explanation.surface: Fabric chosen to captivate a stylish dowager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engross' looks like a container signal but the five words just supply their first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Tweed is a rough woollen cloth, a kind of fabric.

clue.text: Unfair treatment in coverage is mentioned

indicators.note: in says the answer is contained within the following words

parts.note: spans the end of coverage, the whole of is and the start of mentioned

explanation.surface: Discrimination is raised in the news coverage.
explanation.definitionFit: Ageism is discrimination against people because of their age, a form of prejudice.

clue.text: He praises grown-up protecting article when confronted by men

indicators.note: being confronted by something puts it face to face, here directly after
something protecting another wraps around it

explanation.surface: An adult shielding an item when faced by men offers praise.
explanation.walkthrough: OR (other ranks) is the crossword staple for men, i.e. soldiers who are not officers.
explanation.definitionFit: An adulator flatters and fawns, a person who heaps praise.

clue.text: Party game requires subtle diplomacy at first, nothing lacking

indicators.note: at first puts this section ahead of the game in the answer
subtle suggests something worked cunningly, so the letters are craftily rearranged
lacking says something is missing and must be removed

explanation.surface: A party game needs a little tact to get started, with nothing missing.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove O from the reworked word before rearranging. Plaid Cymru is the Welsh nationalist political party.
explanation.definitionFit: Plaid Cymru is a political party in Wales, so it fits a one-word definition by example.

clue.text: "Strange pleasure, beginning to end, with foreign friend"? Don't believe him!

indicators.note: the first letter is moved to the back of the word

explanation.surface: Someone offering a weird mix of pleasure and foreign friendship is not to be trusted.
explanation.walkthrough: The last part is a cryptic hint for a person, not a definition of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfamiliar means not known, so strange in the sense of new and unknown.

clue.text: Note agents entering decisive contest about money

indicators.note: entering means going inside something else

parts.note: the final is the deciding match
N is the abbreviation for note

explanation.surface: A note is circulating among the agents competing in a deciding contest about cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Financial means relating to money matters.

clue.text: Some of these cards brought over?

definitions.text: Some of these cards brought over?

indicators.note: bringing something over flips it, so the letters run backwards
some of says only part of the following words is used

parts.note: the end of these and start of cards

explanation.surface: A few cards from this hand are passed across.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: aces are some of the cards in a pack.
explanation.definitionFit: Aces are among the playing cards in any pack, the top-ranking ones in most games.

clue.text: See 8
Power to support liberal group of countries defending zone in bad weather

indicators.note: defending something means surrounding and guarding it
in a down clue, a supporting item sits underneath the rest

parts.note: Z is the abbreviation for zone
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: Power is promised to a liberal bloc defending a zone during foul weather.
explanation.walkthrough: The free-plus-EU pair together goes round the Z.
explanation.definitionFit: A freeze-up is a spell of icy weather when everything freezes, so harsh winter conditions.

clue.text: Sea eagle in river

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a coastal bird of prey
second meaning: a river in Ireland flowing through Fermanagh

explanation.walkthrough: 'In' seems to put the bird in water; it just joins two meanings. The Erne is a river in Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: The erne is the white-tailed sea eagle, and the Erne is also an Irish river.

clue.text: Recalled, after doctoring, nursing home, a success in the end?

indicators.note: nursing means holding close, so one piece is cradled inside another
doctoring means tampering with, so the letters are altered

explanation.surface: A patient is remembered, after medical treatment in a nursing home, as finally recovering.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: the fairy-tale heroine rises from drudgery to marry the prince.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cinderella is someone neglected who finally wins recognition, like the fairy-tale heroine.

clue.text: In interlude from duties, referring to Church's Saints

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for saint, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: During a break from work, someone talks about the Church's saints.
explanation.definitionFit: A recess is a break from work, as when parliament or a court adjourns.

clue.text: Political group reduced offer to college in New York

indicators.note: reduced means cut short, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a tender is a bid or offer

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for college

explanation.surface: A political faction cut its offer to a New York college.
explanation.walkthrough: A tendency is a faction within a party, as in Militant Tendency, a hard-left group inside the British Labour Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Tendency names an organised faction within a larger political party.

clue.text: See 1
Delivery signal after break ends early

indicators.note: ending early means the word stops short of its final letter
after places one piece behind the other

parts.note: a cue is a signal to act

explanation.surface: A delivery signal comes after the break is cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: Delivery can mean being saved from danger, so it is a synonym for rescue.

clue.text: Republic's friend

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the People's Republic in East Asia

explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is'. In cockney rhyming slang 'china plate' rhymes with mate, so china is a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: China is a republic in Asia, and in British slang a mate or close friend.

clue.text: Repulsive using lady — heartless

indicators.note: removing the heart leaves only the outside letters of each word

explanation.surface: A cruel woman who exploits others is repellent.
explanation.definitionFit: Ugly means unpleasant to look at or offensive, which is what repulsive describes.

clue.text: Din from hooter I stopped

indicators.note: a thing stopped by something is plugged, with that item sitting inside

parts.note: hooter is British slang for the nose

explanation.surface: I silenced the racket coming from a car horn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hooter' looks like a car horn, the obvious source of din, but it is slang for nose.
explanation.definitionFit: A din is a loud unpleasant racket, which is noise.

clue.text: Big attraction of publication isn't me unfortunately!

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A writer laments that the star feature of a magazine is someone else.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnetism is powerful attraction, literal or personal charm.

clue.text: Ruin I passably reinterpreted with participation of lecturer here?

definitions.text: Ruin I passably reinterpreted with participation of lecturer here?

indicators.note: reinterpreted means read in a new way, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for lecturer

explanation.surface: A lecturer gives a passable new interpretation of an ancient ruin at the site.
explanation.walkthrough: Salisbury Plain in Wiltshire, England, holds Stonehenge, the ruin that a lecturer might reinterpret there.
explanation.definitionFit: The ruin of Stonehenge stands on this chalk plateau in southern England, so the whole clue points to the place.
